behavior: A device attention feed that carries only systemAlerts (empty work-item and group layers) must keep those alerts through the shared Rust/UniFFI decode, so the app can show them instead of the all-clear state a genuinely empty feed produces (EI-24766495996412373).

repo.worktreeNote: crates/papercup-core/tests/client_test.rs carried an uncommitted peer rustfmt reformat of the relay/fallback tests at run time; the two attention tests below were not part of that diff.

runs.role: behavior under test: an alert-only feed keeps its systemAlerts through decoding
contrast case: a feed with no alerts and no work decodes to empty system_alerts
neighbouring decode coverage, not bound to this clause

framework: cargo (integration test against a wiremock device API)
command: report-cargo-tests over papercup-rust-mobile crates/papercup-core with filter attention_, PAPERCUSP_CARGO_DISK_ALARM_PERCENT_FLOOR_BYPASS_GB=60 (cargo target volume at 99% use, 95 GiB free)
oracle: Hand-authored JSON fixtures served by wiremock at /api/device/attention (bearer-token matched, expect(1)). The alert-only test asserts the decoded feed keeps exactly one system alert with id, kind, severity, title and body equal to the fixture literals, alongside empty work items and zero group count, with an unknown additive field (futureMetadata) tolerated. The contrast test asserts a feed without systemAlerts decodes to empty system_alerts. Expected values are literals in the test, not output of the code under test.
scopeLimit: This proves the shared Rust decode layer preserves an alert-only feed. The Swift needs-attention verdict over that feed is covered separately by ios/PapercupTests/AttentionFeedTests.swift (testSystemAlertOnlyFeedNeedsAttention, testEmptyLegacyFeedIsAllClear), which ran in macOS CI run 37524303501 and is not bound by this record.
